tests/test.sh:153-180 sends SIGTERM to the old group, waits at most five seconds, launches a replacement, then accepts any HTTP response on port 3000. It never requires the old group to exit, new PID liveness or the new PID to own the response. The startup probe at 42-57 also treats HTTP errors as ready.
quality.counterexample: A SIGTERM-resistant old server (or unrelated listener) keeps answering port 3000 while replacement exits with EADDRINUSE. The helper returns ready=1 and restart_mcp.py:47 reports success, so the judge may mistake old in-memory state for persisted post-restart state or wrongly fail a correct app.
quality.suggested_fix: In the shared restart template, prove the old group exited, the new PID remains live and owns a fresh health response; return an error when replacement fails, then rerun bounded resistant-process fixtures.
